headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors from shared file-based workflows; compliance and leakage are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files, screenshots, and files from supported macOS apps, while Mentat reads selected files and uses filesystem-based workflows. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent’s output is saved into files the other ingests. The pathway is not fully default, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs text into a file that agent_b later reads as task context
IF the operator copies agent_b diffs into files that agent_a ingests from macOS apps
mitigations: Keep agent_a and agent_b on separate workspaces
Disable automatic file handoff between agents
Review any file content before passing it across agents
Use plain-text summaries instead of raw artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files exchanged between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while agent B touches selected source files and can write them back. If both operate on the same workspace, sensitive code or screenshots can flow from A into B’s outputs. B’s broad model-provider egress increases exposure, but the profiles do not prove uncontrolled exfiltration, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or folder
IF agent_a is given screenshots or uploaded files containing secrets
mitigations: Use separate repositories or clones per agent
Remove secrets from shared files before handoff
Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive paths
Turn off screenshot sharing unless needed
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its shared state is via filesystem. ChatGPT Desktop can read files and also works with app context and files, so the pair can collide on the same repo without locking. The rubric flags unrestricted shared writes plus git mutation as high; uncertainty about exact coordination should escalate, not reduce.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF agent_b commits or rewrites files while agent_a is reading them
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Serialize edits with a simple lock file
Have only one agent write at a time
Review git diffs before applying them
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals and can modify git state, so if it consumes ChatGPT Desktop’s output as authoritative, mistakes can propagate into committed code. ChatGPT Desktop can also ingest files and app context, making it easy for one agent’s output to become the other’s input without verification. That default workflow is dangerous enough for high.
conditions: IF agent_b applies edits derived from agent_a without independent review
IF agent_a’s file-derived summary is treated as ground truth by agent_b
mitigations: Require a human review step before applying diffs
Ask agent_b to restate assumptions before editing
Cross-check claims against source files
Limit agent_b to generating proposals only
requires-engineering: add automated verification tests before commit

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not show a clear residency or certification mismatch. The main compliance concern is that agent_a handles screenshots, voice, uploaded files, and connected IDE code, while agent_b handles source files and model-provider keys; that can create policy friction if regulated data is placed in shared code workflows. The other agent is cited because the risk is about the pair’s combined handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into files or screenshots shared between the agents
IF organizational policy forbids sending source code to the configured model provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Confirm provider and retention settings before use
Avoid screenshots containing sensitive data
Use a non-regulated sample project for testing
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for the pair
